observed: One many-sided circular counter stands on an isolated timber floor patch with paper margins.
Boxy token monitors hang around a central pole above occupied stations, corded phones, desk lamps and long ticker-paper strips.
A raised-arm phone caller contrasts with seated workers and a sleeper; a frog on a lily-pad form stands over a marked gold-coloured gauge, and one station has a small flag.
Storage and paper stacks fill the counter's centre and the station fronts, making it look used rather than uniform.
corrections: Give the sleeping station a visible lamp that is off; the image does not supply one clearly.
Replace coloured or arrow-tipped price lines with a single brass price line and faint scale, and remove orange accents.
The frog and its base are not brass; only a gauge bound to a labelled synthetic reading may use brass, with engraved marks.
Treat the flag only as the named waiting-for-owner state; do not introduce token flags or an activity highlight.
Resolve the actual counter envelope, station spacing and figure ratio in the proportions round, with the picked character bodies.

Colour audit 13 October: the sampled brass gauge/counter pair is only 1.010:1; adjust it to meet the proposed 1.5:1 separation on its actual mount. Lift dark glass, steel, timber and jacket faces for near-black 3:1 outlines; preserve the sampled visible timber range, which locally reaches 2.933:1. Remove paper writing and lamp glow.
